### Enable AOF with appendonly yes

Source: https://github.com/redis/docs/blob/main/content/operate/oss_and_stack/management/persistence.md

Enables the append-only file (AOF) persistence strategy in the Redis configuration file. When enabled, every command that changes the dataset is appended to the AOF and replayed on restart to rebuild state.

```plaintext
appendonly yes
```

--------------------------------

### Mount local data directory for persistence

Source: https://github.com/redis/docs/blob/main/content/operate/oss_and_stack/install/install-stack/docker.md

Starts Redis with a local volume mounted to /data, storing all data in the local-data directory on the host.

```bash
$ docker run -v /local-data/:/data --name redis -p 6379:6379 redis:<version>
```

--------------------------------

### Redis cache configuration with maxmemory and maxmemory-policy

Source: https://github.com/redis/docs/blob/main/content/operate/oss_and_stack/management/config.md

Use this configuration to set Redis as a cache with a maximum memory limit of 2 megabytes and an allkeys-lru eviction policy. This allows Redis to evict keys using an approximated LRU algorithm when the memory limit is reached, without requiring the application to set explicit expirations.

```redis
maxmemory 2mb
maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru
```

--------------------------------

### Test connection with PING

Source: https://github.com/redis/docs/blob/main/content/operate/oss_and_stack/install/install-stack/snap.md

Use the PING command in redis-cli to test the connection. The expected response is PONG.

```bash
127.0.0.1:6379> PING
PONG
```

--------------------------------

### Connect with redis-cli from Docker container

Source: https://github.com/redis/docs/blob/main/content/operate/oss_and_stack/install/install-stack/docker.md

Runs redis-cli inside the running Redis container. Use this when redis-cli is not installed locally.

```bash
$ docker exec -it redis redis-cli
```
